jobs.role: Analyst, Office of Regulatory Relations (Bank Regulatory Engagement)
jobs.salary: About $75,000 – $105,000 (per aggregator; not shown on the GS page)
jobs.summary: Goldman's Office of Regulatory Relations manages the firm's relationships with its regulators and sets the standards for every regulatory interaction across the firm. The Bank Regulatory Engagement analyst supports exams and regulator requests, tracks remediation work, keeps up with relevant laws and rules, flags issues that need escalating, and follows up with teams across the firm to get information in on deadline. Requirements are a bachelor's degree, strong writing and Office skills, and familiarity with financial products. It's tagged early-career on Goldman's site.
jobs.fit_rationale: This is a real entry-level regulatory job at a top bank, and it uses all three parts of her background: Holland & Knight regulatory tracking and briefings, DeGette casework that meant chasing agencies and keeping clean records, and credit-union experience with financial products and operational controls. It's compliance-flavored work rather than lobbying, so it fits if she's open to financial regulation. NYC, in office.

jobs.category: Energy policy / defense energy resilience (gov contractor)
jobs.summary: CTC is a nonprofit federal contractor. Its Energy, Resilience and Sustainability Division helps DoD and other federal clients make military installations energy-resilient. The associate analyst researches energy-resilience efforts, energy procurement options and on-site generation technologies, compiles and analyzes electricity and fuel data, turns lessons learned into policies and strategies for federal energy and water goals, and supports client relationships. The posting asks for 0–4 years of experience.
jobs.fit_rationale: This is a genuinely entry-level energy policy role that also touches defense, two of her top priorities. Her Holland & Knight energy, infrastructure and national-security research and her DeGette energy-access casework fit well. Three things to know: the posting leans quantitative (Excel and data, with Tableau/GIS a plus), it requires U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain a Secret clearance (an active clearance isn't required), and the pay range only reaches $75k+ in its upper half. This is today's defense-adjacent pick.

The associate supports sponsorships and tradeshows, CRM, tours and events, the budget, and day-to-day team operations. The posting calls it a foundational step for a career in public policy, government relations, advocacy and business development. It asks for about 1 year of experience, and part-time work while in school counts.

Her National Security & Defense sector-group support at Holland & Knight and her Hill internship (with a Colorado member) fit directly, and her experience running the budget and systems for her student organizations covers the operations side.
